stories.headline: Designing an AI serving harness built to last
stories.summary: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark scores.
stories.why_it_matters: Those advances have been extraordinary. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it.
Technical Implementation: For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark scores.

Deployment & Impact: But as AI moves from experimentation to production, the question facing enterprise leaders has changed—it’s no longer, “what can the model do?”—it’s now, “Can we deliver that intelligence reliably, economically, and at scale?” Increasingly, the answer depends on the serving harness—the engineering system surrounding the model, including the architecture, memory management , scheduling, and optimization decisions that determine how efficiently model intelligence becomes a production capability.

stories.headline: A 1,000-mile cloud on Mars may reveal physics never seen in nature
stories.summary: Every morning during the Martian spring and summer, a thin and extremely long cloud emerges, only to disappear again. The wispy formation appears near the volcano Arsia Mons and gradually elongates until it reaches over 1,000 miles—about the distance from New York to Kansas City as the crow flies—before dissipating.
stories.why_it_matters: This cycle then repeats for several months. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.
key_points: Problem & Context: Every morning during the Martian spring and summer, a thin and extremely long cloud emerges, only to disappear again.

Technical Implementation: Since it was first recorded by a probe in 2018, scientists have been unable to find a plausible explanation for the existence of this cloud, often referred to as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC).

Deployment & Impact: Recently, researchers successfully modeled the cloud’s formation for the first time, their results suggesting that it may be driven by a physical process that has never been directly observed in any planet's atmosphere.

stories.headline: Single-tenant Titus: VM-level isolation on a multi-tenant container platform

stories.headline: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
stories.summary: On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad - whether it's a still image, video, audio, or text - that "has been significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence" to include a label in the same format as the ad itself.
stories.why_it_matters: That applies to TV commercials from multi-billion-dollar companies , as well as restaurants' ugly, crowded flyers about their wing specials. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.

stories.headline: Introducing Amazon ECS Gateway: A fully-managed ingress solution for ECS services
stories.summary: When platform teams manage containerized applications at scale on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) , configuring ingress networking for each service often becomes a bottleneck. For every new service, teams must provision and connect Application Load Balancers (ALBs) , AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificates, AWS WAF web ACLs, and security groups, then keep those resources in sync as services scale, update, or operate.
stories.why_it_matters: This per-service overhead slows down deployment velocity and increases the risk of configuration drift across an organization. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cloud.

stories.headline: Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
stories.summary: A video player seeking to the middle of a movie asks for a few megabytes. Under our old range caching, that one request could make Cloudflare pull 128 MiB from the origin and move it between data centers, sometimes after the viewer had already left.
stories.why_it_matters: Range requests are how large files get delivered, and caching them naively easily leads to wasted network bandwidth and wasted disk operations when running a CDN at scale. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cloud.
key_points: Problem & Context: Under our old range caching, that one request could make Cloudflare pull 128 MiB from the origin and move it between data centers, sometimes after the viewer had already left.
Technical Implementation: Range requests are how large files get delivered, and caching them naively easily leads to wasted network bandwidth and wasted disk operations when running a CDN at scale.
Deployment & Impact: For R2, Cloudflare's object storage, p99 time to first byte dropped by about half, and a follow-up improvement cut tiered cache traffic for R2 and similar workloads by about 6%.

stories.headline: Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
stories.summary: Today, Cloudflare is launching a post-quantum geographically restricted key manager in support of our Data Localization Suite (DLS) in closed beta. This new PQ GeoKey Manager is a cornerstone of Cloudflare’s data sovereignty solutions, making sure that a customer's decryption keys are only accessible in their chosen geography.
stories.why_it_matters: GeoKey Manager implements this by wrapping each decryption key such that it can only be decrypted by Cloudflare servers that are located in the allowed geography. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cloud.
